title: Seminar 3
section: A format matched to the contribution
text:
A format matched to the contribution
01New evidence supports a research article or communication.02Critical synthesis supports a review.03An argued direction may support a perspective.04Reusable data support a data paper.05A testable future plan supports a research proposal.

title: Seminar 3
section: Five formats and their central questions
text:
Five formats and their central questions



Format
Reader’s central question




Review
What does the body of evidence establish?


Communication / Letter
What focused new result matters now?


Perspective
Which direction deserves investigation, and why?


Data paper
Can I understand, trust and reuse this dataset?


Research proposal
Can this plan test an important question?

title: Seminar 3
section: A review needs a synthesis method
text:
A review needs a synthesis method
01Define the question and boundaries.02Document the search and selection approach.03Compare studies on compatible bases.04Explain agreements, conflicts and evidence gaps.I&EC Research: Author Guidelines

title: Seminar 3
section: A communication needs a complete focused argument
text:
A communication needs a complete focused argument
01A narrow claim can fit a short format.02Essential controls and limitations still belong in the paper.03Length limits and urgency criteria depend on the journal.04Correspondence comments on published work and serves another purpose.I&EC Research: Author Guidelines

title: Seminar 3
section: A perspective develops an evidence-based position
text:
A perspective develops an evidence-based position
01State the position and intended audience.02Use evidence to explain why the direction matters.03Address plausible counterarguments.04Separate established findings from proposed directions.Organic Process Research & Development: Author Guidelines

title: Seminar 3
section: A data paper makes a dataset reusable
text:
A data paper makes a dataset reusable
01Document acquisition and processing.02Provide variable definitions, units and identifiers.03Demonstrate technical quality and known limits.04Explain access, versioning and reuse conditions.Scientific Data: Submission Guidelines

title: Seminar 3
text:
One result, different writing tasks
01Research article: test the catalyst modification with adequate controls.02Review: explain why comparable studies disagree about deactivation.03Proposal: test whether the modification changes the rate of deactivation.The format follows the contribution and the available evidence.

title: Seminar 3
section: A proposal links a hypothesis to a decision
text:
A proposal links a hypothesis to a decision
01Question: does the modification slow deactivation?02Hypothesis: the modified catalyst loses activity more slowly.03Test: compare independent batches under controlled feeds.04Decision: estimate a degradation-rate difference and its uncertainty.

title: Seminar 3
section: Controls and feasibility belong in the proposal
text:
Controls and feasibility belong in the proposal
01Check transport effects before interpreting intrinsic kinetics.02Plan independent batches and justify sample size.03Define calibration, exclusion and analysis procedures.04State milestones, risks and a feasible fallback.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Workshop: choose a defensible format
8minutes01Groups, 8 minutes. Use Worksheet 3A.02Classify four research situations.03Give one reason and one missing requirement for each.04Identify a plausible alternative format.

title: Seminar 3
text:
A one-page proposal outline
01Question and current evidence gap02Hypothesis and primary outcome03Experimental design and comparison basis04Analysis, uncertainty and decision rule05Feasibility, risk and fallback

title: Seminar 3
text:
Proposal clinic
7minutes01Write a 90-second pitch from your outline.02A partner identifies the strongest alternative explanation.03Revise the control or measurement that addresses it.

title: Seminar 3
section: A proposal needs a result that could refute it
text:
A proposal needs a result that could refute it
01Hypothesis: the modification reduces the deactivation rate.02Primary comparison: rate difference between independent catalyst batches under matched conditions.03If the uncertainty still includes no meaningful improvement, the result does not support the engineering claim.Define a meaningful effect and analysis plan before collecting data.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Common mismatches
01A literature list without synthesis is an incomplete review.02A short manuscript still needs adequate evidence.03A dataset without metadata is hard to reuse.04A proposal needs a test and a criterion for interpreting results.

title: Seminar 3

11 percentage points at one condition
01Conversion: 64% to 75% at 350 °C02Absolute increase: 11 percentage points03Relative increase: 11 / 64 = 17.2%04The experiment does not establish mechanism or industrial lifetime.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Journal fit and trust
01Scope and recent papers identify the audience.02The contribution must match an accepted article type.03Check the journal identity, editorial process and fees on official pages.04A metric alone cannot establish fit or research quality.I&EC Research: Author Guidelines

title: Seminar 3
text:
Editorial and peer review decisions
01Initial checks assess the submission package.02Editors assess suitability and select reviewers.03Reviewers evaluate the scientific evidence.04The editor decides whether to accept, revise or reject.Springer Nature: Editorial process

title: Seminar 3
text:
Cover letter structure
01Manuscript title and article type02Main finding with its scope and magnitude03Relevance to the journal’s readers04Accurate declarations required by the journalSpringer Nature: Cover letter

title: Seminar 3
section: A claim an editor can evaluate
text:
A claim an editor can evaluate
01Weak: “Our revolutionary catalyst transforms industrial production.”02Revised: “At 350 °C, the modified catalyst increased mean conversion from 64% to 75% across three independent batches per condition.”03Limit: “Testing covered one feed composition and an 8 h observation period.”

title: Seminar 3
text:
A complete cover-letter paragraph
01We submit “Catalyst modification under matched conditions” as a research article.02At 350 °C, mean conversion increased from 64% to 75% across three independent batches per condition.03The comparison addresses catalyst performance under a defined feed. Testing covers one feed and an 8 h observation period.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Workshop 1: a short cover letter
8minutes01Pairs, 8 minutes. Use Worksheet 1A.02Write 120–150 words for a plausible target journal.03Include one quantified finding and one limitation.04Exchange drafts and mark unsupported claims.

title: Seminar 3
text:
The submission package
01Author list, affiliations and approval02Manuscript, figures and supporting information03Data and code availability, funding and conflicts04Required declarations, reviewer details and final file checks

title: Seminar 3
section: A response that can be checked
text:
A response that can be checked
01Reviewer comment, reproduced accurately02Direct answer with the supporting evidence03Change made in the manuscript04Exact location in the revised versionNature Computational Science: How to respond to reviewers

title: Seminar 3
text:
Agreement and justified disagreement
01Agree: revise the claim and identify the change.02Partly agree: address the valid concern and explain the remaining limit.03Disagree: give evidence and a reasoned alternative.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Workshop 2: the stability claim
8minutes01Reviewer: “Eight hours cannot establish industrial durability.”02Write a response and a replacement manuscript sentence.03Specify what the current data support.04Propose a next experiment without claiming that you ran it.

title: Seminar 3
section: A response with a traceable change
text:
A response with a traceable change
01Reviewer: “Eight hours cannot establish industrial durability.”02Response: We agree. We have removed the industrial-durability claim and limited the conclusion to the observation period.03Revised text: “The test covers 8 h under the reported conditions. Longer-term durability remains untested.”Teaching example. Add the actual page and line numbers after revising the manuscript.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Submission readiness review
01A reader can trace every main claim to evidence.02The package meets the target journal’s instructions.03Responses cover every substantive reviewer concern.04Any unresolved requirement has an owner and next action.

title: Seminar 3
section: A caption that defines the evidence
text:
A caption that defines the evidence
01Conversion at 350 °C for baseline and modified catalysts under matched feed and flow conditions.02Points show three independent catalyst batches per condition. Large markers show means. Error bars show ±1 SD.03The comparison covers one feed composition. The experiment does not establish a reaction mechanism.Synthetic teaching data. Report the remaining operating conditions in the final caption or linked methods.

title: Seminar 3
section: A caption should support independent reading
text:
A caption should support independent reading
01What system and comparison does the figure show?02Which conditions, units and normalization apply?03What is n, and what counts as an independent replicate?04What do points, lines and uncertainty marks mean?

title: Seminar 3
text:
Workshop: redesign one figure
10minutes01Pairs, 10 minutes. Use Worksheet 2A.02Choose a scientific claim and a suitable display.03Sketch the axes, units, raw observations and uncertainty.04Write a caption and identify one unsupported interpretation.

title: Seminar 3
section: Tables preserve exact values and conditions
text:
Tables preserve exact values and conditions
01Put units in the headers.02Use precision that the measurement supports.03Distinguish missing, not measured and not applicable.04Keep each row’s basis of comparison explicit.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Figure integrity and reproducibility
01Keep raw data unchanged and document exclusions.02Generate the figure from a saved script.03Use consistent scales for panels meant for comparison.04Retain source files, processing steps and permissions.

title: Seminar 3
section: Peer review of the revised figure
text:
Peer review of the revised figure
6minutes01Can you identify the claim within 20 seconds?02Can you reconstruct the comparison from the caption?03Does the display show variation and limitations?04What would you ask the author to change?

title: Seminar 3
section: Technical repeats do not create new batches
text:
Technical repeats do not create new batches
01Design A: one catalyst batch, measured nine times.02Design B: three independently prepared batches, each measured three times.03For between-batch variation, Design B has n = 3 independent batches.

title: Seminar 3
section: A readable export is part of the evidence
text:
A readable export is part of the evidence
01Check the figure at its intended publication size.02Use the lab palette and redundant markers or labels.03Export vector files or raster files at ≥600 dpi.04Check embedded PDF fonts and exclude Type 3 fonts.

Generative AI and research ethics
PhD Seminar · Chemical EngineeringA verifiable and accountable AI workflow28 October 2026   12:00–13:00Soorathep Kheawhom

title: Seminar 3
text:
Tasks and verification burden
01Language editing: check meaning and quantitative claims.02Literature support: open and verify the original sources.03Code assistance: test units, assumptions and outputs.04Research interpretation: retain human scientific judgment.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Human responsibility remains central
01AI tools do not qualify as authors under COPE’s position.02Researchers remain responsible for manuscript content.03Journal and institutional requirements both apply.COPE: Authorship and AI tools

title: Seminar 3
section: A claim can change during language editing
text:
A claim can change during language editing
01Input: “Conversion was 75% for one feed at 350 °C.”02Edited output: “The catalyst achieved superior activity under all operating conditions.”03Audit: scope expanded, comparator missing, activity undefined.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Verification before reuse
01Trace each claim to a source or measurement.02Check numerical values, units and denominators.03Read the cited source and confirm it supports the claim.04Save what you accepted, changed or rejected.

title: Seminar 3
text:
An example of publisher-specific disclosure
01Elsevier requires a declaration for substantive AI help in manuscript preparation.02Basic grammar, spelling and punctuation checks are exempt.03AI use within the research method needs a reproducible Methods description.Policy checked 6 October 2026. Recheck the target journal before submission.Elsevier: Generative AI policies for journals

title: Seminar 3
text:
Image categories have different rules
01Elsevier allows explanatory AI images with disclosure.02Data plots must derive faithfully from data and reproducible methods.03AI must not fabricate primary research images.04General-purpose image generators cannot create Elsevier graphical abstracts.Publisher-specific example, checked 6 October 2026.Elsevier: Generative AI policies for journals

title: Seminar 3
text:
Confidentiality before a prompt
01Does the material belong to you, collaborators or a reviewer assignment?02Do you have authority to share it with this service?03What do the service terms say about retention and training?04Use approved tools and the minimum necessary information.

title: Seminar 3
section: A numerical audit catches a changed claim
text:
A numerical audit catches a changed claim
0164% to 75%0211 percentage points0317.2% relative increase04“An 11% increase” changes the denominator and is ambiguous.

title: Seminar 3
text:
A bounded editing prompt
01“Edit this paragraph for clarity. Preserve every numerical value, unit, comparison and limitation. Add no factual claims or references. List changes that may alter meaning.”02The author still checks every change.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Workshop: audit an AI-assisted paragraph
10minutes01Pairs, 10 minutes. Use Worksheet 4A.02Find unsupported scope, numerical and citation claims.03Rewrite the paragraph using only the supplied evidence.04Record an accept, revise or reject decision for each change.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Code needs scientific tests
01Check dimensions and units before trusting an output.02Test a limiting case with a known answer.03Compare against a hand calculation or independent method.04Record versions, dependencies and data provenance.

title: Seminar 3
text:
Three ethics scenarios
6minutes01An AI tool improves the wording but invents a reference.02A collaborator uploads an unpublished industrial dataset.03An image generator creates a plausible SEM micrograph.

title: Seminar 3
text:
A useful AI use record
01Tool and version, date and purpose02Material shared and the authority to share it03Output retained and verification performed04Required disclosure and responsible author

title: Seminar 3
section: An AI use log records the check
text:
An AI use log records the check
01Task: improve the clarity of a nonconfidential paragraph.02Verification: checked every value, unit, comparison, limitation and cited source against the originals.03Decision: restored the tested scope, rejected an invented reference and retained only verified edits.Record the actual tool, date and applicable version. Disclose use as the target journal requires.

title: Seminar 3
section: A disclosure must describe actual use
text:
A disclosure must describe actual use
01Name the tool and the task it performed.02Describe human review and responsibility.03Use the location and wording required by the journal.
